contexts.text: When it pleases the Lord, good Spirits appear like stars... and evil Spirits like balls of charcoal fire.
The life of cupidities and thence of pleasures sometimes appears with evil Spirits like a charcoal fire... AC 4417.
The life of cupidities may be likened to a charcoal fire; the falsities to the dim lumen from it.
A yellow light as from charcoal...
Evil Spirits see... from the light of Heaven; but it is a lumen like that from a charcoal fire, for into such a lumen is the light of Heaven turned when it goes to them.

Spirits who are only in those things which are of the light of the world, and thus in falsities from evils, do indeed have light from Heaven; but a light of a fatuous character, and such as comes from burning charcoal or a firebrand.
They who are in evil and thence in falsities appear in a lumen as of a charcoal fire... AC 4418.

In Hell there is not indeed darkness, but there is a dim lumen, like that which comes from a charcoal fire... AC 4533. AC 7870:2. HH 131 [Swedenborg footnote 1.], References. HH 481:4. HH 553:end. HH 584.

When the Rational is subjected to sensuous things, falsities are in the centre and truths in the circumference; the things which are in the centre are in a sort of lumen there, but in a fatuous lumen, or like that which arises from a charcoal fire... it is this lumen which is called darkness...
The infernals are indeed in lumen... but it is like the lumen from a dry charcoal fire...
They have no light in their caverns except one resembling the light from live coals or from burning charcoal.
The light in Hell is also of three degrees; the light in the lowest Hell is like the light from burning charcoal...
In their own light, which is like the light from burning charcoal, (devils) do not appear as monsters, but as men.
They have a life such as that of a dim fire, a charcoal one...
The rational things of others, who are still more darkened by falsities, (appear) like charcoal fires...
(They presented) flaming fires in a dark chamber where there were coals at one corner...
Yesterday I saw the dry fire of a hearth in the coals... When it was at the driest it approached a charcoal colour, so that there is hardly anything [to be seen] except black charcoal.
A red colour... comes into existence from the flame in Hell which is from the fire there, which fire is like a charcoal fire.
A fire of coal () = evil from man's Own love.
To forge iron with the tongs, and to work in the coal () = to hatch falsities which favour man's Own loves.
